mainTopic: The widow and the heirs: her finds, her work, seizing property for support, losing support through silence, and a parallel rule for a תלמיד serving his רבי.
overview: The amud opens with a proof from שמואל, who says a widow keeps the lost items she finds. The proof tries to show that the משנה reads "הניזונת" and not "ניזונת". The גמרא rejects the proof: a husband gets his wife's finds only to avoid איבה, and that reason does not apply to the heirs. רבי יוסי בר חנינא teaches that a widow does all of a wife's household jobs for the heirs, except the personal ones. In a parallel rule, רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a תלמיד does all of a slave's jobs for his רבי except untying his shoe. רבא and רב אשי narrow that shoe rule, and רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן בר יצחק warn a teacher not to stop his student from serving him. Back to widows: a widow who seized movables for her מזונות keeps them, which is backed by a ברייתא and a real case. רבינא limits this to food and excludes the כתובה; מר בר רב אשי challenges him, and a tradition from רבא backs רבינא. A widow who stays silent for two or three years loses her past מזונות but not her future support. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן asking who must bring proof when the heirs say they paid and she says she got nothing.

steps.title: A proof from שמואל: the widow keeps what she finds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמואל's rule that a widow keeps her own finds. It argues this fits the reading "הניזונת" but clashes with the reading "ניזונת".
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי זירא said in the name of שמואל, "A widow's find belongs to herself." If the משנה says "הניזונת" (the one who is supported), that works well. But if it says "ניזונת" (she is supported), then the heirs should be just like the husband. A wife's find goes to her husband, so here too the widow's find should go to the heirs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of שמואל to help decide which wording of the משנה is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only some widows are supported ("הניזונת"), שמואל could be talking about a widow who is not supported, so of course her finds are hers. If every widow is supported ("ניזונת"), the heirs seem to fully replace the husband. Since a wife's finds go to her husband, a widow's finds should go to the heirs, and that contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is about to bring a source as proof

steps.confusionAlert: The difference between "הניזונת" and "ניזונת" is just one letter, ה. But it changes the meaning a lot: "the widow who is supported" (only some) versus "a widow is supported" (always).

phrases.english: Come and hear,
Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said:
A widow's found item belongs to herself.
Granted, if you say
we learned "the one who is sustained," it works well.
phrases.notes: This is the wording debate from before: with the ה, only some widows get support, so שמואל can mean a widow who doesn't.

phrases.english: But if you say we learned "is sustained,"
let them (the heirs) be like the husband:
just as with a husband, a wife's find goes to her husband,
here too, the wife's find should go to the heirs!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier debate over whether the משנה reads "הניזונת" or "ניזונת".
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה reads "הניזונת" (not every widow is supported).
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's rule (said by רבי זירא) that a widow's find belongs to herself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the heirs always support her, they replace the husband, so they should also get her finds.

steps.title: Rejection: the husband's right to her finds is only about avoiding bad feelings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the reading "ניזונת". It explains that a husband gets his wife's finds only to prevent איבה, and that reason does not apply to heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you the משנה says "ניזונת". Why did the חכמים say a wife's find goes to her husband? So she will not face his bad feelings toward her. As for these heirs, let them have bad feelings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It shows that שמואל's rule fits even the reading "ניזונת".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that whoever supports the woman automatically gets her finds. The גמרא says no: the husband gets her finds for a special reason, to keep peace in the home. The חכמים are not worried about peace between the widow and the heirs, so her finds stay hers.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you: the opening of a rejection that keeps the original position

steps.whatToRemember: A husband gets his wife's finds only because of איבה (keeping peace at home). Heirs do not get that special rule, so a widow keeps her own finds, even if the משנה reads "ניזונת".

phrases.english: Actually, I will tell you:
we learned "is sustained":
What is the reason the Sages said
a wife's find goes to her husband?
So that she should not face hostility.
These, let them have hostility.
phrases.notes: "These" means the heirs. If they're upset with the widow, the חכמים don't mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof. שמואל's rule fits both readings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the husband gets her finds just because he supports her. In fact the reason is preventing איבה, which does not apply to heirs.

steps.title: What jobs a widow does for the heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא rules that a widow does all the jobs for the heirs that a wife does for her husband, except the personal ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: All the jobs a wife does for her husband, a widow does for the heirs. The exceptions are pouring his cup, making his bed, and washing his face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching on the same topic: how much a widow must work for the heirs who support her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general the heirs do take the husband's place, so she owes them the usual household work. But the jobs that show closeness between husband and wife are left out. They belong only to a husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the heirs are like the husband in money and work matters, but not in the close, personal side of marriage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
All tasks that a wife does for her husband,
a widow does for the heirs,
except for pouring the cup
and making the bed
and washing his face, hands, and feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the widow's finds to the work she does for the heirs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow does all a wife's jobs for the heirs, except pouring the cup, making the bed, and washing his face, hands and feet.

steps.title: What a student does for his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a parallel rule: a תלמיד does all the jobs an עבד does for his master, except untying his shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: All the jobs a slave does for his master, a student does for his teacher, except untying his shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: A similar "all jobs, except" teaching, this time about a תלמיד and his רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the previous rule, it starts with a full list of jobs taken from one relationship and then removes one. The job removed is untying the shoe, a lowly job that marks someone as a slave.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
All tasks that a slave does for his master,
a student does for his teacher,
except for untying (his) shoe.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching with the same "all jobs, except" pattern as step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד does all a slave's jobs for his רבי, except untying his shoe.

steps.title: The shoe rule applies only where the student is not known
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. A תלמיד avoids untying his רבי's shoe only where people don't know him, since there he could be mistaken for an עבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We only said this where people do not recognize the student. But where they recognize him, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule from the previous step about a student not untying his teacher's shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that people will see the student untying the shoe and think he is a slave. If people already know who he is, nobody will make that mistake, so the rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a phrase that narrows an earlier rule)
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Rava said:
We said this only
phrases.notes: "This" is רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that a student does not untie his teacher's shoe.

phrases.english: in a place where people do not recognize him,
but in a place where people recognize him
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on untying the shoe applies only where the student is not recognized.

steps.title: Even among strangers, wearing תפילין removes the problem
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי narrows the rule further. Even where the student is unknown, the problem exists only if he is not wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even where they don't recognize him, we only said this when he is not wearing תפילין. If he is wearing תפילין, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second limit on top of רבא's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד does not put on תפילין. A student wearing תפילין is clearly not a slave, so nobody will make the mistake even in a strange place.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And even in a place where people do not recognize him,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא מַנַּח תְּפִלִּין,
phrases.english: we said this only when he is not wearing tefillin,
but if he is wearing tefillin,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין אוֹתוֹ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to רבא's limit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student wearing תפילין may untie the shoe even where he is unknown.
steps.whatToRemember: The shoe rule is only about not being mistaken for a slave. Where that mistake can't happen, because he is known or wears תפילין, the rule falls away.

steps.title: Stopping a student from serving withholds kindness from him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a teacher who stops his student from serving him is like one who withholds חסד from him. He learns it from a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who stops his student from serving him is as if he withheld kindness from him, as it says, "לַמָּס מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד."
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of students serving teachers, רבי יוחנן now speaks to the teacher. He warns him not to refuse his student's service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Serving a teacher is a chance for the student to do חסד. A teacher who refuses that service takes this chance away from him. The פסוק is read as "one who withholds from his friend, withholds kindness."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Anyone who prevents his student from serving him
is as if he withheld kindness from him,
as it is stated: "To him that withholds from his friend, kindness"
phrases.notes: איוב 6:14. The word לַמָּס is read like "מונע", meaning the one who holds back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַמּוֹנֵעַ תַּלְמִידוֹ מִלְּשַׁמְּשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the student's duty to the teacher's side of the same relationship
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher should not stop his student from serving him; doing so withholds חסד.

steps.title: He also takes away the student's fear of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that such a teacher also removes יראת שמים from the student. He learns it from the end of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says: He even removes fear of Heaven from him, as it says, "וְיִרְאַת שַׁדַּי יַעֲזוֹב."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק builds on רבי יוחנן's teaching and makes it stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the teacher takes away חסד. רב נחמן בר יצחק says he takes away even יראת שמים, since serving a teacher builds a student's awe of Heaven. He reads it from the next words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says:
He even removes from him the fear of Heaven,
as it is stated: "And the fear of the Almighty he forsakes."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק in איוב 6:14.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר: אַף פּוֹרֵק מִמֶּנּוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger result to רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stopping a student from serving also strips him of יראת שמים.
steps.whatToRemember: Serving one's רבי is valuable for the student himself. A teacher should let him serve.

steps.title: A widow keeps movables she seized for her support
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that if a widow grabbed movable property for her food, what she seized stays hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A widow who seized movables for her support, what she seized, she seized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of a widow's support from the heirs. It brings a new ruling from רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a widow who did not wait for the court and took movable property from the estate to pay for her food. רבי אלעזר says the heirs cannot take it back from her. Once she holds it, it counts as validly collected.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
A widow who seized movable property for her sustenance,
what she seized, she seized.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אַלְמָנָה שֶׁתָּפְסָה מִטַּלְטְלִין בִּמְזוֹנוֹתֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the student topic and returns to the widow and the heirs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Movables a widow seized for her support remain in her possession.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says word for word what רבי אלעזר said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: A widow who seized movables for her support, what she seized, she seized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי אלעזר's ruling by showing a ברייתא with the same wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is a teaching from the time of the תנאים, so it carries more weight. Finding the same rule there shows that רבי אלעזר's ruling is well founded.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)

phrases.english: That is also taught in a baraita:
A widow who seized movable property for her sustenance,
what she seized, she seized.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a widow keeps seized movables

steps.title: A real case: the חכמים could not take back the seized bag of coins
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a real case. רבי שבתי's daughter-in-law seized a bag full of coins, and the חכמים could not take it from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, when רב דימי came, he said: There was a case with רבי שבתי's daughter-in-law, who seized a bag full of coins, and the חכמים did not have the power to take it from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support for רבי אלעזר's ruling. This time it is a story of what actually happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She grabbed a bag of coins, which is movable property. The חכמים could not force her to give it back. This matches the rule that a widow keeps what she seized.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר:
phrases.english: And likewise, when Rav Dimi came, he said:
There was an incident with Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law,
who seized a saddlebag full of coins,
and the Sages did not have the power
to take it out of her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a real case as further support
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a widow keeps seized movables
steps.raayaSupportSource: A מעשה reported by רב דימי
steps.whatToRemember: A widow who has already seized movables for her support keeps them. Three sources say so: רבי אלעזר, a ברייתא, and a real case.

steps.title: רבינא limits the rule to seizing for food
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the rule that the widow keeps what she seized applies only to seizing for מזונות. If she seized movables as payment of her כתובה, בית דין takes them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We only said this about food. But if she seized it for her כתובה, we take it away from her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא puts a limit on רבי אלעזר's rule from Step 9. The widow keeps what she grabbed only if she grabbed it for food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said that a widow who grabs movable property keeps it. רבינא says that rule covers only grabbing for מזונות. If she grabbed movables to pay off her כתובה, the seizure does not work, and בית דין takes the property back.

keyTerms.meaning: For food or support. Here it means seizing property to pay for her living costs.
The marriage contract payment a widow collects from her husband's estate.
We take it out of her hands.
We only said this when... (a phrase that limits an earlier rule).

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not arguing with רבי אלעזר. He agrees with the rule but says it covers only seizing for food.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
We only said this regarding sustenance,
phrases.notes: "This" is רבי אלעזר's rule from before: what she seized stays hers.

phrases.english: but for the marriage contract, we take it away from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לִמְזוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of רבי אלעזר, which the ברייתא and רב דימי's case supported, to seizing for food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seizing movables for מזונות works. Seizing movables as payment of the כתובה does not, and בית דין removes them.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי asks why the marriage contract should be different
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי argues that מזונות and כתובה are alike, since both are paid only from land. So if seizing movables works for food, it should also work for the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי challenged this: Why is the כתובה different? Because it is paid from land and not from movables? Food is also paid from land and not from movables! Rather, just as for food, what she seized she keeps, so too for the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי attacks רבינא's limit from Step 12. He argues that food and the כתובה should follow the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only possible reason to treat the כתובה differently is that it is collected only from land, so movables seized for it should be returned. But מזונות are also collected only from land, and still her seizure for food works. So her seizure should work for the כתובה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it. Used when a later אמורא attacks an earlier statement.
What is the difference? Why treat this case differently?
Movable property, things that can be carried.
What she seized, she seized. She keeps it.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi challenged it:
What is different about the marriage contract,
that it is paid from land and not from movables?
phrases.notes: He is guessing רבינא's reason: since the כתובה is collected only from land, grabbing movables shouldn't count.

phrases.english: Sustenance is also paid from land and not from movables!
Rather, for sustenance, what she seized she keeps,
so too for the marriage contract!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's distinction between food and כתובה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's ruling that movables seized for the כתובה are taken back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food and the כתובה are both paid only from land. Since seizing movables works for food, it should also work for the כתובה. There is no real difference.

steps.title: רבא is reported to agree with רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר נפתלי tells רבינא that his ruling was also said in the name of רבא, which supports him against the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר נפתלי said to רבינא: This is what we say in the name of רבא, just like you.
steps.whatsHappening: After the challenge in Step 13, רב יצחק בר נפתלי backs up רבינא. He reports that רבא taught the same ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not answer מר בר רב אשי's logic. Instead it adds weight to רבינא's view by citing an earlier authority, רבא, who ruled the same way: movables seized for the כתובה are taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of. Passing on a teaching from someone else.
Like you, in agreement with you.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on movables seized for the כתובה. רבינא (and רבא) say they are taken back. מר בר רב אשי says she keeps them, just as with food.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר נַפְתָּלִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Naftali said to Ravina:
This is what we say in the name of Rava, like you.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמְרִינַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא כְּווֹתָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא against מר בר רב אשי's challenge by citing a tradition from רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's ruling that movables seized for the כתובה are taken back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition taught in the name of רבא, reported by רב יצחק בר נפתלי.

steps.title: A widow who waits years without asking loses her support
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן זמרא, teaches that a widow who waited two or three years without demanding מזונות has lost them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: A widow who waited two or three years and did not ask for food has lost her food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about widows' מזונות. If she waits a long time without asking, she loses her right to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about a widow who took property on her own. Now the case is a widow who did nothing at all. Since she never asked, she is assumed to have given up her right, and רבי יוסי בן זמרא says flatly that she has lost her מזונות. רבא will later limit this to the past (step 19).

keyTerms.meaning: She waited, she let time pass.

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule opens a new discussion that the גמרא will go on to examine.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
A widow who waited two or three years
and did not demand sustenance,
has lost sustenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching. It moves from a widow who seized property to a widow who never asked for support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow who waited two or three years without demanding מזונות loses her right to them.

steps.title: Why say three years if two is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: if she loses her מזונות after two years, there is no need to mention three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if after two years she already lost it, do we need to say three?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the rule from step 15. If two years is already enough to lose her מזונות, then 'or three years' seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'two or three years' looks extra: if two silent years are already enough to lose her right, then three years obviously are too. The גמרא assumes every word in a teaching has a purpose, so it asks what 'three' is teaching us.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, given that... (it opens a 'this is obvious' type of question)
Is it needed? (meaning, it should go without saying)

phrases.english: Now, if after two years she lost it,
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יוסי בן זמרא's words 'two or three years' from step 15.

phrases.english: is it necessary to say three?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא שְׁתַּיִם — אִיבְּדָה, שָׁלֹשׁ מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the מימרא in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'two or three years' in רבי יוסי בן זמרא's teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two years is enough to lose the right, three years is obviously included, so mentioning it adds nothing.

steps.title: Two years for a poor woman, three for a rich one
steps.stepSummary: The two numbers describe two different women. A poor widow loses her right after two years, and a rich widow only after three.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it is talking about a poor woman, and there about a rich woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'two' and 'three' are not repeating each other. Each number fits a different kind of widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor widow needs food urgently, so if she stays quiet for two years, she must have given up her claim. A rich widow can live on her own money for a while, so her silence only shows she gave up after three years.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (opens an answer)
Here... there (splitting the rule into two cases)

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here, with a poor woman,
phrases.notes: The poor woman is the 'two years' case. She can't go that long without asking unless she gave up.

phrases.english: there, with a rich woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בַּעֲנִיָּה, כָּאן בַּעֲשִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two numbers into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Two or three' looked like one rule with an extra number.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two years applies to a poor widow and three years to a rich widow.

steps.title: Or: two years for a bold woman, three for a modest one
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: a widow who is not shy about asking loses her right after two years, and a modest widow only after three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: here it is talking about a bold woman, and there about a modest woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to explain the two numbers. This time the difference is the widow's personality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bold widow would have demanded her food quickly, so two silent years show she gave it up. A modest widow is embarrassed to ask the יתומים, so her silence is only treated as giving up after three years.

keyTerms.meaning: A bold woman who is not shy about demanding her rights
A modest woman who is shy about asking

phrases.english: Alternatively: here, with a bold woman,
there, with a modest woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: כָּאן בִּפְרוּצָה, כָּאן בִּצְנוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same קשיא, as an alternative to step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two numbers into two different cases, this time by personality
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Two or three' seemed to be one rule with an extra number.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two years applies to a bold widow and three years to a modest widow.

steps.title: She loses only the past support, not future support
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the rule: the widow loses her claim only for the years that already passed. From now on, she can still receive מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We only said this about the past, but going forward she does have support.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how far the rule of losing מזונות goes. She can't collect for the silent years, but her right to future support stays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her silence is treated as giving up only the support for the time she kept quiet. It does not cancel her right to be supported, so once she asks, the יתומים must support her from then on.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about... (introduces a limit on a rule)
Backward, for the time already passed

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the widow never loses her basic right to מזונות through silence. She only loses the back payments.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: Rava said: We said this only for the past,
phrases.notes: He means she can't demand payment for the years she supported herself.

phrases.english: but from now on she has it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְמַפְרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבי יוסי בן זמרא's rule from step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiting two or three years makes the widow lose only her claim for past support. She is still entitled to support from now on.

steps.title: Who must prove whether the widow got her support?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks: if the יתומים say they gave the widow her מזונות and she says she got nothing, which side has to bring proof?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked: The orphans say 'We gave,' and she says 'I did not take.' Who has to bring proof?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן raises a new question about a dispute between the widow and the יתומים. The גמרא is setting up a discussion about which side carries the burden of proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a claim the other denies, and there is no evidence. The question is whether the יתומים must prove they paid, or whether the widow must prove she was not paid.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised an unresolved question

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan asked:
If the orphans say: We gave,
and she says: I did not take,
upon whom is it to bring proof?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יְתוֹמִים אוֹמְרִים נָתַנְנוּ, וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא נָטַלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about proof in disputes over the widow's מזונות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the יתומים must prove they paid, or the widow must prove she was not paid.
